clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country in March 1952, within the following year: June grew anxious and homesick, writing daily to her sister left behind; Walter stayed out in the orchard from dark to dark while June kept to her bed for weeks that first winter; Glen began fighting at his new school; Walter and his brother Harlan stopped speaking over their father's land money; Walter and June fought over money for new trees. By September 1953, June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, her anxiety easing as she found her footing.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failing in May 1968 when the late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter drank heavily most nights; he and Glen blamed each other for the loan; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Carl's asthma worsened that winter; your bed-wetting began in April 1969; your grandmother Ida's heart trouble was found in May 1969. By October 1969, Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, his functioning rising as the immediate crisis passed.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the following year: Glen sat in the truck in the yard for hours, his functioning down; you stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; you kept to your room and grew distant from your mother; loud fights between Glen and Marian over money broke out most nights; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Walter began drinking again after six years sober; Carl spent most nights at his girlfriend's house. By June 1976, you were eating again and made the track team, your functioning rising as your father found steady work driving a delivery truck in March.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into your house in January 1990: you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals; you worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows while Hollis took his mother's side; Owen began having tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; you developed eczema flaring on both hands; you and Hollis fought most nights. By June 1991, when Wilma took a flat in town, the eczema cleared over the summer and the household settled.
